messages:
Incident Bot: :rotating_light: PAGING: High error rate + tail latency on /v1/embeddings in us-west-2 (affected customers: subset of enterprise tenants). Pager: Ashok (oncall).
Ashok (oncall): I got the page. I'm looking at dashboards now — error rate is ~12% at peak, p50 fine but p95/p99 huge.
Maria (eng-sre): Jumping in. Correlating with autoscaler logs and KV-cache metrics.
Ashok (oncall): Quick ask: can we bump Dedicated pool capacity as an emergency throttle? If it's a load spike we can add nodes, else it might worsen if cache misses drive more load.
Evan (infra): Autoscaler reports a flapping event around 03:12 UTC — scale-up attempt failed due to node boot timeout (NTP issue on image). Rolling back left us at lower capacity.
Jamie (product): Any customer-facing failures? Lina, CS — are you seeing support tickets?
Lina (support): Two high-priority tickets from enterprise customers mentioning timeouts when generating embeddings. CS is handing the first one; will notify of impact.
Maria (eng-sre): Observed KV cache hit ratio dropped from 92% -> 28% coincident with a spike in sequence lengths. That increased per-request compute and triggered autoscaler. But the autoscaler failed to stabilize.
Ashok (oncall): Ok mitigation plan: 1) temporarily route heavy embedding requests to fallback smaller model variant for non-SLA customers, 2) disable autoscaler aggressive policy, 3) manually add 4 nodes to Dedicated pool if image boot fixes. @Evan can you patch the node image?
Evan (infra): On it. I have a temporary node image rollback in progress and will force a scale-up after it's ready. ETA 12 mins.
DevOps Team: Adding a temporary rate-limiter at the edge for the embeddings route for unauthenticated/client-headers to protect core customers. Config applied: 
```
route: /v1/embeddings
limit: 80rps
scope: client-id
fallback: model-emb-small
```
Ashok (oncall): After rate-limiter and fallback, errors dropped to ~1.5% and latency p99 improving. Customers with dedicated SLAs still on primary path.
Customer Success: Notified affected customers via status page and DM. Major customer A acknowledged mitigation, asking for RCA.
Maria (eng-sre): We're stabilizing. Creating incident channel for root cause. We'll need a postmortem: probable chain = KV cache hot prefix behavior + longer seq lengths -> autoscaler scale-fail -> capacity shortfall -> routing fallback pressure.
Jamie (product): Schedule a postmortem. Preferably tomorrow 1000 UTC. Who owns?
Ashok (oncall): I can do initial timeline + incident write-up. Maria to own technical RCA. Evan to own infra/autoscaler change. Jamie for customer comms. Lina for support impact log.
Incident Bot: Incident created: INC-2026-178950 (status: resolved -> monitoring). Postmortem meeting requested for 1789584800 (2026-03-16 10:00 UTC).
Maria (eng-sre): Action items I'm assigning now:
- Maria: deep-dive on KV cache eviction patterns + synthetic test for prefix-heavy workloads.
- Evan: fix node image NTP/boot sequence; add unit test to infra CI.
- Ashok: update autoscaler backoff logic and add a canary rollout.
- DevOps Team: add an alert for KV cache hit ratio < 70% for >5m.
- Jamie: update public status page postmortem note and coordinate with CS.
- Lina: compile list of affected tenants + support tickets.

Ashok (oncall): Proposed alert tuning snippets to reduce noise and page only when impact is customer-visible:
```
alert: embeddings_error_rate_p95
expr: (sum(rate(embeddings_errors[1m])) by (cluster) / sum(rate(embeddings_requests[1m])) by (cluster)) > 0.05
for: 5m
labels:
  severity: page
annotations:
  runbook: /runbooks/embeddings-high-error
```
Maria (eng-sre): Add a secondary condition to only page when affected_tenants_count > 0 to avoid paging on canary tests. Also add a graceful alert that goes to Slack only (no page) for short blips.
Evan (infra): Infra mitigation completed — new image rolled back and 6 nodes successfully booted. Autoscaler will be disabled for 10m while we validate.
DevOps Team: Implemented KV cache hit ratio alert and a synthetic synthetic-embeddings-checker that runs 5m cadence per region.
Lina (support): CS updated customers, provided ETA for RCA. Two tenants asked for estimated time — gave 48h for full RCA.
Jamie (product): Postmortem items to cover in meeting: timeline, customer impact, infra root cause, autoscaler telemetry gaps, detection blind spots, monitoring & runbooks, action owners.
Ashok (oncall): Postmortem meeting invite sent. Owners should attach any logs/queries to the doc before the meeting. I'm starting the timeline doc now.
Maria (eng-sre): Preliminary root cause summary (attach to doc later): unusual shift in request composition (longer text prefixes) -> KV cache thrash -> cache miss storms -> request amplification -> autoscaler triggered scale attempts -> node boot failures -> capacity gap -> fallback/rate-limit invoked -> customer errors.
Evan (infra): Follow-ups for infra: add health-check that fails fast on NTP issues, add node boot metrics to alert if boot > 6m, create pre-warm pool for critical customers.
DevOps Team: Proposed monitoring changes post-incident:
- New metric: kv_cache_effective_hit_ratio (windowed, by prefix).
- Alert: kv_cache_effective_hit_ratio < 75% for 10m -> page SRE.
- Adjust embeddings error-rate page threshold from 5%->8% but add tenant-count guard.
- Synthetic test: embed-synth from 3 regions, assert p95 < 500ms and error_rate < 0.5%.

Ashok (oncall): I'll own the SLO adjustment proposal: suggest keeping current SLOs but add a tiered alerting model (page only on sustained breach + tenant impact). Draft will be in the postmortem doc.
Maria (eng-sre): Assigning follow-up Jira tickets now:
- INF-3421 fix-node-image-ntp (Evan)
- SRE-5118 autoscaler-backoff (Ashok)
- SRE-5120 kv-cache-metrics (Maria)
- OPS-2249 synthetic-embeddings-checker (DevOps Team)
- CS-1187 customer-impact-report (Lina)

Customer Success: Noted. We'll share affected tenant list and any contractual impact.
Jamie (product): Thanks all. Quick reminder: update runbooks with explicit fallback routing steps and customer-communication templates.
Ashok (oncall): Closing note: incident marked resolved at 1789504800. Follow-ups tracked; postmortem scheduled. If anyone finds additional customer-impact data, paste into the doc thread. :pray:
